title: Why airplane food tastes so bland

scenes.say: Why does airplane food taste so bland?
scenes.visual: Meal tray drops in, BLAND stamp slams on it on the word bland

scenes.say: It's not the chef. It's your tongue.
scenes.visual: Chef hat gets crossed out, tongue pops in with a red circle

scenes.say: Planes keep the cabin pressure like you're on a mountain, about eight thousand feet up.
scenes.visual: Altitude gauge counts up to 8,000 ft, mountain silhouette draws in

scenes.say: And the air is drier than most deserts, so your nose dries out. And smell is most of flavor.
scenes.visual: Humidity meter drains, cactus vs plane, nose icon, 'smell = flavor' card

scenes.say: Studies found salty and sweet taste drop by up to thirty percent up there.
scenes.visual: Big -30% counter, two bars shrinking: salt, sweet

scenes.say: Then the engine roar dulls your taste buds even more.
But one taste survives. Umami. That's why people suddenly order tomato juice on planes.
scenes.visual: Bars for salt/sweet stay low, umami bar stays tall; tomato juice slides in

scenes.say: So airlines quietly add extra salt and spice, just to make it taste normal.
scenes.visual: Phone mockup of the tray, EXTRA SALT stamp

scenes.say: Follow for more things you never noticed.
scenes.visual: Big FOLLOW, step badge, bobbing plane
